article.headline: How claude-video turns a clip into evidence Claude can inspect
article.lead: A video tutorial contains two accounts of what happened: the steps visible on screen and the explanation in the audio. The /watch tool makes both available to Claude as frames and a transcript.

sections.heading: What the tool hands to Claude

paragraphs.text: In the local workflow, /watch samples timestamped frames and pairs them with captions or a transcript. If a presenter says “click here,” Claude can use a frame to identify the menu and the transcript to recover the instruction. The important design choice is when to sample: two screenshots on either side of a brief pop-up may both miss it.

picks.question: When a crucial step lasts only a moment, which frame-sampling setting captures it at an acceptable input cost?
